task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: Can the teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile be identified as the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types?
How many absence spells and independent cases are needed to test redistribution of play-type initiations?
Which confounders and selection effects threaten attribution of gained initiations to a specific teammate?
Is the nearest-profile teammate prediction testable with 11 cases and 148 spells?
evidence_establishes: No earlier study records were returned by retrieve_history, so no prior finding about this question is established by this project's records.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether nearest-profile teammates gain the most primary-type initiations after an absence.
Any effect size, direction, or reliability of redistribution for this question.
Whether the required play-type and initiator attribution is accurate enough for the test.
own_inferences: The question as posed is a disjunctive definition: 'closest pre-absence initiation profile' or 'most minutes, initiations, or same-position minutes'. Without one pre-specified similarity metric, the test has multiple routes to a favourable result.
With 11 cases, the effective sample for a case-level claim is about 11, even though there are 148 spells. Spells within a case are not independent.
Chance of the top-ranked teammate being the largest gainer depends on roster size. A hit rate must be compared with that chance level, not with 50%.
Derived initiator and play-type labels come from play-by-play coding and may be unstable for low-volume players, so both the profile and the gain measure are noisy.
uncertainties: Number of eligible teammates per spell, and how many spells have a stable pre-absence baseline.
How many absences fall in the playoffs, which are partial for 2025-26 before 2026-06-21.
Whether [source]-derived play-type records match the raw play-by-play at the level needed.
Roster and coaching changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26 that may confound redistribution.

historical_effect.explanation: retrieve_history returned an empty list, so no [prior work] changed the decision. The decision rests on the task's own design constraints: 11 cases, a disjunctive definition of the predictor, and a noisy derived outcome.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 11 independent cases are available. Spells within a case are clustered, so 148 spells do not give 148 independent tests of the nearest-profile claim.
Absences are not random. Teammates who gain usage may have been selected by the same events that caused the absence, such as injury or role changes.
Initiation and gain are derived from play-by-play labels and graph records, so the outcome depends on the labelling pipeline.
The disjunctive predictor (profile, minutes, initiations, or same-position minutes) allows several definitions to be tried until one fits.

prior_work.summary: No earlier work was retrieved, so it is not known whether this question has already been answered by this project. No prior work is relied on.

risks.text: 11 cases give very little power for a case-level claim. Only a strong and consistent effect would be detectable.
Pre-absence initiation profiles estimated from a few games or low-volume players are unstable, so the nearest-profile ranking may be noise.
Primary play types for many absent players have few initiations, so gain estimates per teammate are sparse.
Large post-absence gains may reflect regression to the mean or selection of teammates who were already rising, not the profile match.
Minutes, coaching changes, lineup changes, and co-absences can drive usage gains independently of profile similarity.
Mis-attributed initiators in play-by-play coding would bias both the profile and the gain measures.
Several profile definitions and gain windows could be compared, inflating the chance of a spurious match.
Under chance, the top-ranked teammate is the largest gainer at roughly 1 divided by roster size, which is low. The test must be scored against that base rate.
Usage and roster structure change across 2022-23 to 2025-26, so pooled comparisons may mix different eras.
Without placebo comparisons, a pattern found in absent-player spells could also appear in comparable non-absence periods.
[source]-derived play-type records could contain join or deduplication errors that create or hide gains.

design.estimand: For each absence spell, whether the teammate ranked most similar on a single pre-specified profile metric is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types, compared with chance given roster size. Secondary: the rank of that teammate among all teammates.
design.unit: Absence spell, nested within the 11 cases (absent-player cases). Analysis is at the case level, with spells as repeated observations.
design.sample: 148 spells from the 11 cases, using only spells with a stable pre-absence baseline. Exclude spells with too few pre-absence initiations. Report the number of spells dropped and the reason for each.
design.power: Scored as top-1 hit rate against chance, 1 divided by eligible teammates. With 11 independent cases, only a large and consistent hit-rate excess is detectable. Report the minimum detectable hit rate before running the test.
design.controls: Pre-specify one profile metric (initiation mix over a fixed pre-absence window) and one gain window. Control for minutes, lineup, and co-absence. Use a leave-one-case-out check. Compare with placebo teammates and with non-absence windows.
design.falsification: Random teammate ranking within roster, same-minutes ranking, and placebo windows with no absence. The profile hypothesis must beat these baselines, not just chance.
design.multiplicity: Single primary metric fixed in advance. Alternative profile definitions reported as exploratory only, with correction if any are tested formally.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the pre-specified nearest-profile teammate beats chance and the placebo and minutes baselines at the case-cluster level, with a permutation p-value and consistent direction across most cases. Otherwise report as uncertain or rejected.
design.data_version: 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoffs, plus 2025-26 regular season only after 2026-04-13. Exclude the 2025-26 playoffs before 2026-06-21 because they are partial. Record the data pull date.
